subject: The full data request to the Town Accountant
asks_for: The itemised request in notes/generated/DATA-REQUEST.md — the MUNIS reports that would close the coverage matrix — sent with the discrepancy review (scripts/build_discrepancy_review.py) as a second attachment.
why: The largest single request this project has made, and the one the modelling rests on: it is what would let the money be followed from appropriation to ledger without inference. Both attachments are generated by this repository, so what was asked for is reproducible rather than remembered.
quote: I spent many hours figuring out how to make a solid request for specific data. … This will let me model everything I’m looking to model. I’ve already modeled a huge amount of the flow, but significant gaps remain that this data will close.

subject: The School Committee minutes that were never posted
asks_for: Copies of 35 sets of School Committee minutes missing from the town’s AgendaCenter — 9 meetings in calendar 2024, 16 in 2025 and 10 in 2026 — each named in the email by date with the direct link to its posted agenda.
why: THE STRONGEST-EVIDENCED REQUEST THIS PROJECT HAS SENT, because every item is a meeting the town itself announced: the agenda is posted and the minutes are not, so each line cites the town’s own URL rather than our inference. Our independent count agrees that the shortfall is real — /boardcompare has the School Committee at 51.6% of 155 meetings minuted, and FY2023 at 0 of 40. It matters beyond tidiness: search_minutes.py can only find what exists, so an unminuted meeting reads as "nobody said it", and for most of these the only surviving record is a recording this project machine-captions, which is a finding aid and not a record.
quote: Can I please have a copy of the meeting minutes that are missing from the Lunenburg Agenda site, through 2024? … 2024 — 9 of 36 posted. 2025 — 16 of 46 posted. 2026 — 10 of 24 posted.

subject: Select Board minutes for FY2025 and FY2026
asks_for: The Select Board minutes the town holds for FY2025 and FY2026 but has not posted, and whether regular posting is planned.
why: MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED. /boardcompare counts what the town itself published: the Select Board minuted 38 of 39 meetings in FY2023 and 41 of 45 in FY2024, then 28 of 49 in FY2025 and 38 of 59 in FY2026 — 97%, 91%, 57%, 64%. That is 42 meetings across the two years asked for with no minutes posted. Minutes are the only record of what was decided for anyone who cannot watch a three-hour meeting, and this archive can only search documents that exist.
quote: the minutes are the only way for people to know what’s going on in the meetings without needing to watch the full 2-3 hour meetings and to know what was decided, officially, at the meetings.

to: Dr. Jodi Fortuna, Superintendent of Schools; school administration
subject: Ski co-op: what the other towns actually paid
asks_for: The revenue received from Leominster, Narragansett and Littleton for the ski programme — and, if no payments were received, the Athletic Director’s emails billing those towns.
why: We hold what was BILLED and nothing about what was RECEIVED. The ski co-op sheet prices every town’s share — Leominster $7,966.29 for nine athletes, Littleton and Narragansett $560.14 each to the town plus $325 from the athlete — and it is a sheet somebody assembled, not a printout from the books (rule 13a). Whether any of it arrived is the difference between a programme that recovers its cost from other towns and one that does not, and no document here answers it.
quote: what I’m looking for is how much Lunenburg brought in from the other towns outside of Lunenburg. … And if there are no payments, can you send me the emails from the AD sent to the other towns requesting the payment?

to: Jennifer Warren-Dyment, Town Manager; Dr. Jodi Fortuna, Superintendent of Schools
subject: PEC agreement
asks_for: The Health Insurance Public Employee Committee (PEC) agreement — the instrument the town and its unions bargain health insurance under.
why: The PEC agreement is what governs whether plan design and contribution splits can be changed at all, and /health-insurance models changing them. Its absence is the difference between “the town could do this” and “the town could do this if the agreement allows it”. It is also not published: not in the town’s collective bargaining folder (DocumentCenter/Index/78) and not in the school’s contracts folder.
quote: Do you have the Health Insurance PEC agreement document, and can you send that to me? I’m told this exists, but I cannot find it posted anywhere.

subject: The General Fund Appropriations schedule for FY2024 and FY2025
asks_for: The General Fund Appropriations / Summary & Classification of Accounts schedule for FY2024 and FY2025 — the same table the annual report printed every year through FY2023 — or the MUNIS year-end expense report by department for those two years.
why: The town stopped printing it after FY2023, so there is no published figure for what any department was appropriated or spent in FY2024 or FY2025. The FY2024 report still carries the warrant’s omnibus budget, which is what was VOTED rather than what was used; FY2025 carries neither. This is the single largest published series this archive has and it stops two years short.
